ustav.title: Устав на Република Северна Македонија
ustav.note: Adopted 17 November 1991. Arts. 62-63 (Assembly of 120 to 140 deputies, four-year term, elections in the last 90 days of the term or within 60 days of a dissolution), 73-74 (referendum), 80-81 (President, five-year term, two rounds), 104 (Judicial Council), 114-117 (municipalities, forms of neighborhood self-government, and the City of Skopje).

amandmani.title: Амандмани на Уставот на Република Северна Македонија
amandmani.note: Amendment XXVIII (2005) makes the Judicial Council 15 members, 8 of them elected by judges from among themselves; Amendment XXXI (9 January 2009) lets a presidential runoff winner take office if more than 40% of voters voted, replacing the earlier majority-turnout rule of art. 81(5).

izboren_zakonik.title: Изборен законик (Службен весник на Република Македонија бр. 40/2006, со измените)
izboren_zakonik.note: The Electoral Code of 2006 governs presidential, Assembly, and local elections and the State Election Commission. It replaced the Law on the Election of Members of the Assembly (2002), the Law on Local Elections, and the Law on the Election of the President. The Commission's site carries the consolidated text; on 17 November 2026 it answered automated clients with a Cloudflare browser challenge (HTTP 403).

dik.title: Државна изборна комисија: избори и резултати
dik.note: The Commission's results archive for presidential, Assembly, and local elections and referendums, with results by electoral district, municipality, and polling station for recent elections. On 17 November 2026 the site and its results subdomain answered automated clients with a Cloudflare browser challenge (HTTP 403).

zls.title: Закон за локалната самоуправа (Службен весник на Република Македонија бр. 5/2002)
zls.note: Adopted 24 January 2002. zgs.title: Закон за градот Скопје (Службен весник на Република Македонија бр. 55/2004)
zgs.note: Adopted 12 August 2004. Art. 19 (the organs of the City of Skopje and of its municipalities are a council and a mayor), art. 20 (the City council has 45 members), art. 21 (who may stand for the City council and mayor).

mls_zto.title: Извештај за оценка на спроведувањето на Законот за територијална организација на локалната самоуправа во Република Северна Македонија
mls_zto.note: Ministry evaluation report, December 2022: SR Macedonia had 34 municipalities from 1982; the 1996 territorial law created 123; the 2004 law created 84; 80 municipalities and the City of Skopje since the merger into Kičevo. Records the failed referendum of 7 November 2004 (turnout 26.58%) and 41 local referendums held from December 2003 to February 2004.

classes.name: Избори за пратеници во Собранието на Република Северна Македонија
classes.note: The Constitution sets 120 to 140 deputies elected for four years (arts. 62-63). In 1994 all 120 were elected in single-member districts in two rounds; in 1998, 85 in single-member districts in two rounds and 35 by proportional representation in one nationwide district; since 2002, 120 in six districts of 20 seats each by closed lists and the D'Hondt divisors, with no threshold. The elections of 2011, 2014, and 2016 added three districts abroad electing one deputy each (123 in all); they were abolished before the 2020 election. Repeat voting at annulled polling stations follows some elections (2008, and Tearce on 25 December 2016). The 1990 Assembly of SR Macedonia is class sobranie_srm.

classes.name: Избори за Собранието на Социјалистичка Република Македонија (1990)
classes.name_en: Assembly of SR Macedonia, first multiparty election (1990)
classes.locator: https://www.sobranie.mk/content/Odluki%20USTAV/UstavSRSM.pdf (the Constitution of 17 November 1991 replaced the constitution of SR Macedonia under which this Assembly was elected)
classes.note: The first multiparty election chose a unicameral Assembly of 120 deputies in single-member districts in up to three rounds (11 and 25 November and 9 December 1990). This Assembly declared sovereignty, called the 1991 independence referendum, and adopted the 1991 Constitution. Earlier assemblies of SR Macedonia were chosen through the Yugoslav single-list and delegate systems (class sobranie_nrm_srm).

dates.note: Third round in the districts still undecided.

classes.name: Избори за претседател на Република Северна Македонија
classes.note: The President is elected directly for five years, at most twice (art. 80). A first-round winner needs a majority of all registered voters; otherwise the two leaders meet within 14 days, and the runoff winner takes office if more than 40% of voters voted (Amendment XXXI of 2009; before it, more than half), or the whole election is repeated (art. 81). The election is held in the last 60 days of the term, or within 40 days of a vacancy. The 2004 election followed President Trajkovski's death; in 1999 the runoff was repeated at polling stations where it had been annulled.

cadence.locator: https://www.sobranie.mk/content/Odluki%20USTAV/UstavSRSM.pdf (art. 81: in the last 60 days of the term, or within 40 days of a vacancy)

classes.name: Избор на претседател на Република Македонија од Собранието (1991)
classes.locator: https://www.sobranie.mk/content/Odluki%20USTAV/UstavSRSM.pdf (art. 80 replaced election by the Assembly with direct election)
classes.note: On 27 January 1991 the Assembly elected in 1990 chose Kiro Gligorov as President by a vote of its deputies; the 1991 Constitution made the office directly elected from 1994.

classes.name: Државен референдум
classes.note: The Assembly calls a referendum by a majority of all deputies, and must call one on the proposal of 150,000 voters; the decision passes if a majority of those voting approve and more than half of all registered voters vote, and binds the Assembly (art. 73). A change of the border needs a majority of all registered voters (art. 74). The 1991 independence referendum was held under SR Macedonia's law; the 2004 referendum on the territorial law and the 2018 consultative referendum on the Prespa agreement both failed on turnout.

cadence.locator: https://www.sobranie.mk/content/Odluki%20USTAV/UstavSRSM.pdf (art. 73: called by the Assembly, or on the proposal of 150,000 voters)

classes.name: Избори за Собранието на НР/СР Македонија (1945-1986)
classes.name_en: Assemblies of PR and SR Macedonia under the Yugoslav single-list and delegate systems (1945-1986)
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen on single People's Front lists and, from 1974, through the Yugoslav delegate system of indirect elections by socio-political chambers; there were no competitive popular contests and the State Election Commission holds no results for them.

classes.name: Сојузни избори на СФР Југославија во Македонија
classes.name_en: Yugoslav federal elections held in Macedonia (1945-1990)
classes.disposition_reason: Elections to the federal assembly of Yugoslavia belong to a Yugoslav polity if the archive adds one, not to North Macedonia's census.

classes.name: Избор на членови на Судскиот совет и на Советот на јавните обвинители
classes.name_en: Members of the Judicial Council and the Council of Public Prosecutors
classes.disposition_reason: Eight of the Judicial Council's 15 members are elected by judges from among themselves and five by the Assembly (Amendment XXVIII); prosecutors elect members of their council the same way. These are internal votes of the judiciary and the Assembly, not public elections, and judges are appointed, never elected by voters.

classes.name: Внатрепартиски избори
classes.disposition_reason: Parties choose their leaders and candidates under their own statutes; the Electoral Code provides for no state-run primaries and the State Election Commission neither runs nor publishes these votes.

classes.name: Совет за развој на планскиот регион
classes.name_en: Councils for the development of the planning regions
classes.disposition_reason: The eight planning regions are statistical and development units with no elected organs; each council for regional development is made up of the region's mayors ex officio.

classes.name: Избори за членови на советите на општините
classes.note: Each municipality is one district; its council of 9 to 33 members by population (law of 2002, art. 34; Kičevo's 23 since 2013) is elected for four years from closed lists by the D'Hondt divisors. The 1996 and 2000 elections were held in 123 municipalities, 2005 and 2009 in 84 (ten of them in the City of Skopje), and since 2013 in 80. A council that is dissolved is replaced by an early election for the rest of the term. The councils of SR Macedonia's 34 municipalities are class sobranie_opstina_srm; the City of Skopje council is class sovet_grad_skopje.

cadence.locator: https://portal.mdt.gov.mk/post-body-files/zakonii-file-1bsL.pdf (art. 35: council members are elected for four years)

classes.name: Избори за градоначалници на општините
classes.note: Each municipality elects its mayor directly every fourth year (law of 2002, art. 49). A first-round winner needs a majority of the votes cast with at least a third of registered voters voting; otherwise the two leaders meet two weeks later and the plurality wins. When a mayor's term ends early, an early election fills it for the rest of the term. The City of Skopje's mayor is class gradonacalnik_grad_skopje.

classes.name: Референдум на ниво на општина
classes.note: The council must call a referendum on a question of municipal competence when 20% of the municipality's voters ask, and may call one itself; the result binds the council (law of 2002, art. 28; procedure in the Law on Referendum and Other Forms of Direct Expression of Citizens). From December 2003 to February 2004, 41 municipalities held non-binding local referendums against their abolition in the territorial reform. No central register of later municipal referendums is published.

classes.name: Избори за членови на Советот на градот Скопје
classes.name_en: Council of the City of Skopje
classes.note: The City of Skopje, a separate unit of local self-government over its municipalities (Constitution art. 117), elects a council of 45 members (law of 2004, art. 20) from closed lists by the D'Hondt divisors in one citywide district, on the same day as the municipal elections. The City had seven municipalities under the 1996 division and ten since 2005.
